title: The tutorials that point you at things
summary: Supermarket Simulator teaches its own systems with small tutorials rather than one help screen: the scale has a tutorial manager with an on-screen indicator and a position for it, and online orders and shoplifters each have a tutorial of their own.
body: The shop is not explained in writing alone. The game carries a tutorial layer with a manager of its own, and the one for the scale arrives with an indicator: a display plus a part that gives that display its position.

An indicator with a position is a pointer. Because the thing shown on screen and the place it belongs are kept as separate parts, a tutorial can point at something in the shop instead of only describing it in text.
Online ordering has a tutorial of its own. That is why the first order is a guided step rather than a screen you have to find for yourself.

Shoplifting has one as well. There is a tutorial for it, an animation listener that belongs to that tutorial and a customer made for it, so the first theft you meet is staged rather than left to chance.
The objectives are kept apart from the tutorials. The game stores tutorial objective data and has a display for it, so what you are being asked to do is a record with something to show it on screen.

Taken together, that is how a new shop is taught: a pointer that leads you to the scale, a first online order walked through with you, and a shoplifter staged for the occasion, each with its own parts rather than one general help panel.
There is a manager over the teaching. An onboarding manager of its own sits above the individual tutorials, which is why a new shop can be walked through rather than only explained.
What this entry does not tell you: how many tutorials there are, when each of them runs, or what any of them gives you. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The scale has a tutorial manager of its own, with an indicator display and a part that holds the indicator's position.
The game carries a tutorial interface rather than only ad-hoc prompts.
Online ordering has a tutorial of its own.
Shoplifting has a tutorial of its own.
That tutorial has an animation listener of its own and a customer made for it.
Tutorial objectives are stored as their own data with a display.
The hint for the tablet is a picture of its own, drawn with the tablet's jobs laid out around it.
The tutorial layer has an onboarding manager of its own.

alt.en: The hint picture the game ships for the tablet: a wheel of its jobs around a tablet, beside a screen showing an online order.
alt.zh: 游戏为平板准备的提示图：平板周围一圈可选工作，旁边是显示线上订单的平板界面。

alt.en: Diagram: a tutorial points at the scale, walks through the first online order, stages a shoplifter, and checks off objectives.
alt.zh: 示意图：教程指向秤、带你完成第一笔线上订单、安排一次小偷事件，并勾选目标。
